title.zh: 卷九十七 志第五十 河渠七
title.raw: 卷九十七 志第五十 河渠七 Volume 97 Treatises 50: Rivers and Canals 7

sentences.zh: 淮郡諸水

translations.literal: Huai commandery various waters
translations.idiomatic: The Waters of the Huai Circuit

sentences.zh: 淮郡諸水：紹興初，以金兵蹂踐淮南，猶未退師，四年，詔燒毀揚州灣頭港口閘、泰州薑堰、通州白莆堰，其餘諸堰，並令守臣開決焚毀，務要不通敵船；

translations.literal: Huai commandery various waters: at beginning of Shaoxing, because Jin troops trampled Huainan, still not withdrawn army, fourth year, edict burn destroy Yangzhou Wantou harbor mouth sluice, Taizhou Jiangyan weir, Tongzhou Baipu weir, remaining various weirs, all order defending officials open breach burn destroy, must not pass enemy boats;
translations.idiomatic: The waters of the Huai circuit: At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, Jin troops were still ravaging Huainan and had not yet withdrawn. In the fourth year, an edict ordered the burning and destruction of the sluice at Yangzhou's Wantou harbor, the Jiangyan weir at Taizhou, and the Baipu weir at Tongzhou; all other weirs were likewise to be breached and burned by the local officials, so that enemy vessels could by no means pass through.

sentences.zh: 又詔宣撫司毀拆真、揚堰閘及真州陳公塘，無令走入運河，以資敵用。

translations.literal: Again edict Pacification Commission destroy dismantle Zhen, Yang weir sluices and Zhenzhou Chen Gong Pond, do not allow enter Grand Canal, to supply enemy use.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict directed the Pacification Commission to demolish the weirs and sluices at Zhen and Yang and Chen Gong Pond at Zhenzhou, lest water be channeled into the Grand Canal for the enemy's benefit.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，詔淮南宣撫司，募民開浚瓜洲至淮口運河淺澀之處。

translations.literal: Fifth year first month, edict Huainan Pacification Commission, recruit people open dredge Guazhou to Huai mouth Grand Canal shallow silted places.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, an edict instructed the Huainan Pacification Commission to recruit civilians to dredge the shallow, silted sections of the canal from Guazhou to the mouth of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，以和州守臣言，開鑿姥下河，東接大江，防捍敵人，檢制盜賊。

translations.literal: Qiandao second year, on Hezhou defending official's words, open excavate Laoxia River, east connect Great River, defend against enemies, control bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiandao, on the report of the prefect of Hezhou, they excavated the Laoxia River, joining it on the east to the Great River to repel enemies and restrain bandits.

sentences.zh: 六年，淮東提舉徐子寅言：「淮東鹽課，全仰河流通快。

translations.literal: Sixth year, Huaidong intendant Xu Ziyin said: "Huaidong salt revenue, entirely relies on river passage swift.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Xu Ziyin, intendant of Huainan East, said: "The salt revenues of eastern Huainan depend entirely on swift passage along the river.

sentences.zh: 近運河淺澀，自揚州灣頭港口至鎮西山光寺前橋垛頭，計四百八十五丈，乞發五千餘卒開浚。」

translations.literal: Recently Grand Canal shallow silted, from Yangzhou Wantou harbor mouth to Zhenxi Xiguang Temple front bridge pile head, totaling four hundred eighty-five zhang, beg dispatch five thousand-plus soldiers open dredge."
translations.idiomatic: The canal has recently grown shallow and silted. From Yangzhou's Wantou harbor to the bridge head before Xiguang Temple west of Zhen, the distance is four hundred and eighty-five zhang in all. I beg that more than five thousand troops be sent to dredge it."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，詔令淮南漕臣，自洪澤至龜山淺澀之處，如法開撩。

translations.literal: Seventh year second month, edict order Huainan transport officials, from Hongze to Guishan shallow silted places, according to law open dredge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year, an edict directed the transport commissioners of Huainan to dredge the shallow stretches from Hongze Lake to Guishan by the established method.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年四月，詔築泰州月堰，以遏潮水。

translations.literal: Chunxi third year fourth month, edict build Taizhou Yue Weir, to check tidal water.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Chunxi, an edict ordered the construction of the Yue Weir at Taizhou to hold back the tide.

sentences.zh: 從守臣張子正請也。

translations.literal: Followed defending official Zhang Zizheng's request.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a petition from the prefect Zhang Zizheng.

sentences.zh: 八年，提舉淮南東路常平茶鹽趙伯昌言：「通州、楚州沿海，舊有捍海堰，東距大海，北接鹽城，袤一百四十二里。

translations.literal: Eighth year, intendant Huainan East Route Ever-Normal Tea Salt Zhao Bochang said: "Tongzhou, Chuzhou along coast, formerly had sea-defending weir, east distance Great Sea, north connect Yancheng, length one hundred forty-two li.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Zhao Bochang, intendant of Ever-Normal Tea and Salt on the Huainan East Circuit, said: "Along the coasts of Tongzhou and Chuzhou there was formerly a sea wall running east to the open ocean and north to Yancheng, one hundred and forty-two li in length.

sentences.zh: 始自唐黜陟使李承實所建，遮護民田，遮罩鹽灶，其功甚大。

translations.literal: First from Tang discipline-and-promotion commissioner Li Chengsi built, shelter protect people's fields, cover shield salt pans, its merit very great.
translations.idiomatic: It was first built by Li Chengsi, the Tang transport and discipline commissioner, to shelter farmland and shield the salt works, and its achievement was very great.

sentences.zh: 歷時既久，頹圮不存。

translations.literal: Time passed long, collapsed ruined not exist.
translations.idiomatic: After long years it had crumbled away and no longer stood.

sentences.zh: 至本朝天聖改元，范仲淹為泰州西溪鹽官日，風潮泛溢，渰沒田產，毀壞亭灶，有請於朝，調四萬餘夫修築，三旬畢工。

translations.literal: Reaching our dynasty Tiansheng inaugural year, Fan Zhongyan as Taizhou Xixi salt official day, wind tides overflow spread, inundate fields property, destroy ruin pavilions pans, had petition at court, mobilize forty thousand-plus laborers repair build, thirty days complete work.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, at the inaugural year of Tiansheng, when Fan Zhongyan was salt commissioner at Xixi in Taizhou, wind and tide overflowed, inundating fields and destroying the salt pans. He petitioned the court, and more than forty thousand laborers were mobilized to rebuild the wall; the work was finished in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 遂使海瀕沮洳瀉鹵之地，化為良田，民得奠居，至今賴之。

translations.literal: Thereupon made sea margin boggy salt-flat land, transform into good fields, people could settle dwell, to today rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the salt flats and boggy ground along the shore were turned into fertile fields; the people could settle in peace, and to this day they rely upon it.

sentences.zh: 自後浸失修治，才遇風潮怒盛，即有沖決之患。

translations.literal: From afterward gradually lost repair governance, just encounter wind tides fierce strong, then have breach rush danger.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward maintenance was gradually neglected, and whenever wind and tide surged violently there was risk of breach.

sentences.zh: 自宣和、紹興以來，屢被其害。

translations.literal: From Xuanhe, Shaoxing onward, repeatedly suffered its harm.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xuanhe and Shaoxing eras onward the region suffered harm again and again.

sentences.zh: 阡陌洗蕩，廬舍漂流，人畜喪亡，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Field paths washed away, houses drifted, people livestock lost dead, are countless.
translations.idiomatic: Field paths were washed clean away, houses were swept off, and the loss of people and livestock was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 每一修築，必請朝廷大興工役，然後可辦。

translations.literal: Each time repair build, must petition court greatly raise labor service, then could be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Each time it was repaired, the court had to be petitioned for a major labor levy before the work could be done.

sentences.zh: 望令淮東常平茶鹽司：今後捍海堰如有塌損，隨時修葺，務要堅固，可以經久。」

translations.literal: Hope order Huaidong Ever-Normal Tea Salt office: hereafter sea-defending weir if have collapse damage, at any time repair mend, must be solid, can endure long."
translations.idiomatic: I hope the Huainan East Ever-Normal Tea and Salt office may be ordered that whenever the sea wall suffers collapse or damage hereafter, it be repaired promptly and made solid enough to endure for the long term."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 九年，淮南漕臣錢沖之言：「真州之東二十里，有陳公塘，乃漢陳登浚源為塘，用救旱饑。

translations.literal: Ninth year, Huainan transport official Qian Chongzhi said: "Zhenzhou's east twenty li, has Chen Gong Pond, is Han Chen Deng dredged source made pond, used rescue drought famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Qian Chongzhi, transport commissioner of Huainan, said: "Twenty li east of Zhenzhou lies Chen Gong Pond. In Han times Chen Deng excavated its source to form this pond and used it to relieve drought and famine.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符間，江、淮制置發運置司真州，歲藉此塘灌注長河，流通漕運。

translations.literal: Dazhong xiangfu period, Jiang, Huai circuit commissioner transport established office Zhenzhou, yearly relied on this pond pour irrigate long river, flow through grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong xiangfu era, when the Jiang-Huai transport commission established its office at Zhenzhou, each year it relied on this pond to feed the long channel and keep the grain transport flowing.

sentences.zh: 其塘周回百里，東、西、北三面，倚山為岸，其南帶東，則系前人築壘成堤，以受啟閉。

translations.literal: Its pond circuit hundred li, east, west, north three sides, lean mountain as bank, its south belt east, then ties former people built rampart made dike, to receive open close.
translations.idiomatic: The pond's circumference is one hundred li. On the east, west, and north its banks lean against the mountains; on the south and east the predecessors built ramparts into a dike to receive the opening and closing of the sluices.

sentences.zh: 廢壞歲久，見有古來基趾，可以修築，為旱乾溉田之備。

translations.literal: Abandoned ruined years long, seen have ancient foundations, can repair build, as drought dry irrigate fields preparation.
translations.idiomatic: It has long lain in ruin, but the ancient foundations can still be seen and may be rebuilt as a reserve for irrigating fields in drought.

sentences.zh: 凡諸場鹽綱、糧食漕運、使命往還，舟艦皆仰之以通濟，其利甚博。

translations.literal: All various salt yards fleets, grain transport, missions coming going, boats all rely on it to pass aid, its benefit very broad.
translations.idiomatic: All salt convoys, grain transport, and missions traveling to and fro depend upon it for passage, and the benefit is very great.

sentences.zh: 本司自發卒貼築周回塘岸，建置斗門、石鹈達各一所，乞於揚子縣尉階銜內帶'兼主管陳公塘'六字，或有損壞，隨時補築，庶幾久遠，責有所歸。」

translations.literal: This office self dispatched soldiers attach build circuit pond bank, established sluice gate, stone barrage each one place, beg at Yangzi county captain rank title within carry 'concurrently supervise Chen Gong Pond' six characters, if have damage, at any time supplement build, may long distant, responsibility have return."
translations.idiomatic: This office has already dispatched troops to reinforce the banks all around the pond and has built one sluice gate and one stone barrage. I beg that the six characters 'Concurrent Supervisor of Chen Gong Pond' be added to the Yangzi county captain's title, so that if there is damage it may be repaired at once and responsibility may rest somewhere for the long term."

sentences.zh: 十二年，和州守臣請於千秋澗置斗門，以防麻澧湖水泄入大江，遇歲旱灌溉田疇，實為民利。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, Hezhou defending official requested at Qianqiu Ravine place sluice gate, to prevent Maoli Lake water leak into Great River, encountering year drought irrigate fields, truly is people's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the prefect of Hezhou requested a sluice at Qianqiu Ravine to keep the waters of Maoli Lake from draining into the Great River, so that in years of drought fields might be irrigated—a real benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 十四年，揚州守臣熊飛言：「揚州運河，惟藉瓜洲、真州兩閘瀦積。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, Yangzhou defending official Xiong Fei said: "Yangzhou Grand Canal, only relies on Guazhou, Zhenzhou two sluices impound accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Xiong Fei, prefect of Yangzhou, said: "The Yangzhou stretch of the Grand Canal depends solely on impoundment at the two sluices of Guazhou and Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 今河水走泄，緣瓜洲上、中二閘久不修治，獨潮閘一坐，轉運、提鹽及本州共行修整，然迫近江潮，水勢沖激，易致損壞；

translations.literal: Now river water runs leak, because Guazhou upper, middle two sluices long not repair govern, only Tide Sluice one seat, transport, salt intendant and this prefecture together carry out repair, yet near river tide, water force rush strike, easy cause damage;
translations.idiomatic: The river water now runs off, because the upper and middle sluices at Guazhou have long gone without repair. Only the Tide Sluice remains; the transport office, the salt intendant, and the prefecture have jointly undertaken repairs, but it lies close to the river tide and the current strikes it hard, so damage comes easily;

sentences.zh: 真州二閘，亦復損漏。

translations.literal: Zhenzhou two sluices, also again damage leak.
translations.idiomatic: and the two sluices at Zhenzhou are leaking again as well.

sentences.zh: 令有司葺理上、下二閘，以防走泄。」

translations.literal: Order officials repair govern upper, lower two sluices, to prevent run leak."
translations.idiomatic: Let the authorities repair the upper and lower sluices to prevent the water from running off."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，淮東提舉陳損之言：「高郵、楚州之間，陂湖渺漫，茭葑彌滿，宜創立堤堰，以為瀦泄，庶幾水不至於泛溢，旱不至於乾涸。

translations.literal: Shaoxi fifth year, Huaidong intendant Chen Sunzhi said: "Between Gaoyou, Chuzhou, ponds lakes vast spread, water-shield plants fill full, ought create establish dikes weirs, to serve impound release, may water not reach overflow spread, drought not reach dry exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxi, Chen Sunzhi, intendant of Huainan East, said: "Between Gaoyou and Chuzhou the lakes and ponds stretch wide and water shield and sedge choke them full. Dikes and weirs should be newly built for impoundment and release, so that in flood the water may not spread unchecked and in drought it may not run dry.

sentences.zh: 乞興築自揚州江都縣至楚州淮陰縣三百六十里，又自高郵、興化至鹽城縣二百四十里，其堤岸傍開一新河，以通舟船。

translations.literal: Beg raise build from Yangzhou Jiangdu county to Chuzhou Huaiyin county three hundred sixty li, again from Gaoyou, Xinghua to Yancheng county two hundred forty li, its dike banks beside open one new river, to pass boats.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that construction be undertaken for three hundred and sixty li from Jiangdu county in Yangzhou to Huaiyin county in Chuzhou, and for two hundred and forty li from Gaoyou and Xinghua to Yancheng county, with a new canal opened along the dikes for the passage of boats.

sentences.zh: 仍存舊堤以捍風浪，載柳十余萬株，數年後堤岸亦牢，其木亦可備修補之用。

translations.literal: Still keep old dike to defend wind waves, plant willows hundred thousand-plus trunks, several years afterward dike banks also firm, its timber also can prepare repair supplement use.
translations.idiomatic: The old dike should be kept to withstand wind and waves, and more than a hundred thousand willows should be planted. In a few years the banks will be firm, and the timber may also serve for repairs.

sentences.zh: 兼揚州柴墟鎮，舊有堤閘，乃泰州泄水之處，其閘壞久，亦于此創立斗門。

translations.literal: Also Yangzhou Chaiyu town, formerly had dike sluice, is Taizhou drain water place, its sluice ruined long, also at this create establish sluice gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Chaiyu town in Yangzhou there was formerly a dike sluice where Taizhou drains its water; the sluice has long been ruined, and a new gate-sluice should be built there as well.

sentences.zh: 西引盱眙、天長以來眾湖之水，起自揚州江都，經由高郵及楚州寶應、山陽，北至淮陰，西達於淮；

translations.literal: West draw Xuyi, Tianchang onward many lakes' water, rise from Yangzhou Jiangdu, pass through Gaoyou and Chuzhou Baoying, Shanyang, north reach Huaiyin, west reach to Huai;
translations.idiomatic: Waters from the many lakes west of Xuyi and Tianchang would be led out, starting from Jiangdu in Yangzhou, passing through Gaoyou and through Baoying and Shanyang in Chuzhou, north to Huaiyin and west to the Huai;

sentences.zh: 又自高郵入興化，東至鹽城而極於海；

translations.literal: Again from Gaoyou enter Xinghua, east reach Yancheng and extreme at sea;
translations.idiomatic: again from Gaoyou into Xinghua, east to Yancheng and on to the sea;

sentences.zh: 又泰州海陵南至揚州泰興而徹于江：共為石鹈達十三，斗門七。

translations.literal: Again Taizhou Hailing south to Yangzhou Taixing and penetrate to river: altogether as stone barrages thirteen, sluice gates seven.
translations.idiomatic: and again from Hailing in Taizhou south to Taixing in Yangzhou and through to the Yangtze—in all thirteen stone barrages and seven gate-sluices.

sentences.zh: 乞以紹熙堰為名，鑱諸堅石。」

translations.literal: Beg take Shaoxi Weir as name, carve on various hard stones."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that it be named the Shaoxi Weir and the name carved on hard stone."

sentences.zh: 淮田多沮洳，因損之築堤捍之，得良田數百萬頃。

translations.literal: Huai fields mostly boggy, because Sunzhi built dikes defend them, obtained good fields several million qing.
translations.idiomatic: The fields of the Huai region were mostly boggy; by building dikes to hold them back he gained several million qing of good farmland.

sentences.zh: 奏聞，除直秘閣、淮東轉運判官。

translations.literal: Memorial heard, appointed Direct Secretariat, Huaidong transport vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was reported, he was appointed to the Direct Secretariat and made vice commissioner of transport on the Huainan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 浙江通大海，日受兩潮。

translations.literal: Zhe River connects Great Sea, daily receives two tides.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe River opens to the great sea and receives two tides each day.

sentences.zh: 梁開平中，錢武肅王始築捍海塘，在候潮門外。

translations.literal: Liang Kaiping period, King Qian Wusu first built sea-defending embankment, outside Chaozhao Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiping era of Liang, King Qian Liu first built a sea wall outside Chaozhao Gate.

sentences.zh: 潮水晝夜沖激，版築不就，因命強弩數百以射潮頭，又致禱胥山祠。

translations.literal: Tidal water day night rush strike, plank rammed not succeed, therefore ordered strong crossbows several hundred to shoot tide head, again sent prayers Xu Mountain shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the tide struck and rammed construction could not hold. He therefore ordered several hundred powerful crossbows to shoot at the tidal bore and also sent prayers to the shrine on Xu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 既而潮避錢塘，東擊西陵，遂造竹器，積巨石，植以大木。

translations.literal: Soon after tide avoided Qiantang, east struck Xiling, thereupon made bamboo vessels, piled great stones, planted with great timbers.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the tide turned aside from Qiantang and struck Xiling to the east. He then made bamboo frames, piled great stones, and set large timbers among them.

sentences.zh: 堤岸既固，民居乃奠。

translations.literal: Dike bank already firm, people's dwellings then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the bank was firm, the people's dwellings were settled.

sentences.zh: 逮宋大中祥符五年，杭州言浙江擊西北岸益壞，稍逼州城，居民危之。

translations.literal: Reaching Song Dazhong xiangfu fifth year, Hangzhou said Zhe River struck northwest bank increasingly ruined, gradually pressed prefecture city, residents feared it.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth year of Dazhong xiangfu in Song, Hangzhou reported that the Zhe River was striking the northwest bank with growing damage and pressing gradually upon the prefectural city, so that the people were in peril.

sentences.zh: 即遣使者同知杭州戚綸、轉運使陳堯佐畫防捍之策。

translations.literal: Immediately dispatched envoy Vice Prefect of Hangzhou Qi Lun, transport commissioner Chen Yaozuo draw defense plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court at once sent envoys together with Qi Lun, vice prefect of Hangzhou, and Chen Yaozuo, transport commissioner, to devise measures of defense.

sentences.zh: 綸等因率兵力，籍梢楗以護其沖。

translations.literal: Lun and others therefore led military strength, deployed fascines and piles to protect its rush.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and the others then led troops and deployed fascines and piles to shield the point of impact.

sentences.zh: 七年，綸等既罷去，發運使李溥、內供奉官盧守懃經度，以為非便。

translations.literal: Seventh year, Lun and others already removed gone, transport commissioner Li Pu, inner palace attendant Lu Shouqin surveyed, considered not suitable.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Lun and the others had left office, Li Pu, transport commissioner, and Lu Shouqin, inner palace attendant, surveyed the works and judged the method unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 請復用錢氏舊法，實石於竹籠，倚疊為岸，固以樁木，環亙可七里。

translations.literal: Requested again use Qian clan old method, pack stones in bamboo cages, lean pile as bank, secure with pile timbers, circuit about seven li.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to restore the old method of the Qian house: stones packed in bamboo cages, piled as a bank and secured with piles, encircling about seven li.

sentences.zh: 斬材役工，凡數百萬，逾年乃成；

translations.literal: Cut timber labor workers, altogether several million, over year then completed;
translations.idiomatic: Timber was cut and labor mobilized to the sum of several million, and only after more than a year was the work finished;

sentences.zh: 而鉤末壁立，以捍潮勢，雖湍湧數丈，不能為害。

translations.literal: And hooked ends wall stand, to defend tide force, although turbulent surge several zhang, could not cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: with the hooked ends standing upright to resist the tide, so that even when the surge rose several zhang it could do no harm.

sentences.zh: 至景祐中，以浙江石塘積久不治，人患墊溺，工部郎中張夏出使，因置捍江兵士五指揮，專採石修塘，隨損隨治，眾賴以安。

translations.literal: Reaching Jingyou period, because Zhe stone embankment accumulated long not governed, people feared drowning, Works Ministry director Zhang Xia went on mission, therefore established river-defending soldiers five commands, exclusively quarry stone repair embankment, as damaged so repair, masses relied thereby at peace.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jingyou era the stone embankment along the Zhe had long gone without repair and the people feared drowning. Zhang Xia of the Ministry of Works went on inspection and established five river-defense commands of soldiers devoted to quarrying stone and repairing the embankment, mending damage as it occurred, so that the people lived in security.

sentences.zh: 邦人為之立祠，朝廷嘉其功，封甯江侯。

translations.literal: Country people for him established shrine, court praised his merit, enfeoffed Marquis Who Pacifies River.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the region built a shrine to him, and the court praised his achievement and enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Pacifies the River.

sentences.zh: 及高宗紹興末，以錢塘石岸毀裂，潮水漂漲，民不安居，令轉運司同臨安府修築。

translations.literal: Reaching Gaozong Shaoxing end, because Qiantang stone bank destroyed cracked, tidal water drifted rose, people not at peace dwell, ordered transport office together Lin'an prefecture repair build.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Gaozong's Shaoxing era the Qiantang stone bank was shattered, the tide flooded upward, and the people could not dwell in peace; the transport office and the Lin'an prefecture were ordered to repair it jointly.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乾道九年，錢塘廟子灣一帶石岸，復毀於怒潮。

translations.literal: Xiaozong Qiandao ninth year, Qiantang Miaozi Bay stretch stone bank, again destroyed by angry tide.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Qiandao under Xiaozong, the stone bank along Miaozi Bay at Qiantang was again destroyed by the raging tide.

sentences.zh: 詔令臨安府築填江岸，增砌石塘，淳熙改元，復令有司：「自今江岸沖損，以乾道修治為法。」

translations.literal: Edict ordered Lin'an prefecture build fill river bank, add lay stone embankment, Chunxi inaugural year, again ordered officials: "From now river bank rush damage, take Qiandao repair governance as model."
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the Lin'an prefecture to fill the river bank and add stone facing to the embankment. At the inaugural year of Chunxi the authorities were again instructed: "Henceforth, whenever the river bank suffers rush damage, the repairs of Qiandao shall serve as the model."

sentences.zh: 理宗寶祐二年十二月，監察御史兼崇政殿說書陳大方言：「江潮侵齧堤岸，乞戒飭殿、步兩司帥臣，同天府守臣措置修築，留心任責，或有潰決，咎有攸歸。」

translations.literal: Lizong Baoyou second year twelfth month, investigating censor concurrently Chongzheng Hall lecturer Chen Dafang said: "River tide gnaws dike banks, beg warn instruct Palace, Step two commissions commanders, together capital prefecture defending officials arrange repair build, attend mind assign responsibility, if have breach rush, blame has where return."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Baoyou under Lizong, Chen Dafang, investigating censor and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, said: "The river tide is eating away the banks. I beg that the commanders of the Palace and Step guards be warned, together with the capital prefectural officials, to arrange repairs, keep responsibility in mind, and know that if there is a breach blame will have somewhere to fall."

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，監察御史兼崇政殿說書李衢言：「國家駐蹕錢塘，今逾十紀。

translations.literal: Third year eleventh month, investigating censor concurrently Chongzheng Hall lecturer Li Qu said: "State resides halt Qiantang, now exceeds ten reign-periods.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, Li Qu, investigating censor and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, said: "The state has made its residence at Qiantang for more than ten reign-periods already.

sentences.zh: 惟是浙江東接海門，胥濤澎湃，稍越故道，則沖齧堤岸，蕩析民居，前後不知其幾。

translations.literal: Only this Zhe River east connects sea gate, Xu tidal bore surges, slightly cross old course, then rush gnaw dike banks, wash scatter people's dwellings, before after not know how many.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zhe River on the east meets the sea gate, and the Xu tidal bore surges forth. Slightly off the old channel, it gnaws the banks and scatters the people's houses—how many times before and after, one cannot say.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，造捍江五指揮，兵士每指揮以四百人為額。

translations.literal: Qingli period, created river-defending five commands, soldiers each command with four hundred people as quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingli era five river-defense commands were created, each command with a quota of four hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 今所管才三百人，乞下臨安府拘收，不許占破。

translations.literal: Now managed only three hundred people, beg issue to Lin'an prefecture muster collect, not allow divert break.
translations.idiomatic: Those now under command are only three hundred. I beg that Lin'an be ordered to muster them and forbid their being diverted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 及從本府收買樁石，沿江置場樁管，不得移易他用。

translations.literal: And follow this prefecture purchase piles stones, along river place depots pile manage, not allow shift other uses.
translations.idiomatic: Let the prefecture also purchase piles and stone, set up riverside depots to manage them, and not allow them to be shifted to other uses.

sentences.zh: 仍選武臣一人習于修江者，隨其資格，或以副將，或以路分鈐轄系銜，專一鈐束修江軍兵，值有摧損，隨即修補；

translations.literal: Still select martial official one skilled in river repair, follow his qualification, perhaps as vice general, perhaps as route seal controller attached title, exclusively control river-repair soldiers, when have damage rush, immediately repair supplement;
translations.idiomatic: Select one martial official skilled in river works and, according to his rank, attach him as vice general or route seal controller, exclusively to command the river-repair troops, so that whenever damage occurs it may be patched at once;

sentences.zh: 或不勝任，以致江潮沖損堤岸，即與責罰。」

translations.literal: If not competent, causing river tide rush damage dike banks, then give responsibility punishment."
translations.idiomatic: and if he is not equal to the task and the tide damages the banks, let him bear punishment."

sentences.zh: 臨安西湖周回三十里，源出於武林泉。

translations.literal: Lin'an West Lake circuit thirty li, source emerges from Wulin spring.
translations.idiomatic: West Lake at Lin'an measures thirty li in circuit; its source is the Wulin spring.

sentences.zh: 錢氏有國，始置撩湖兵士千人，專一開浚。

translations.literal: Qian clan had state, first established lake-dredging soldiers thousand men, exclusively open dredge.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Qian held the realm, a thousand lake-dredging soldiers were first established for exclusive dredging.

sentences.zh: 至宋以來，稍廢不治，水涸草生，漸成葑田。

translations.literal: Reaching Song onward, gradually abandoned not governed, water dried grass grew, gradually became water-shield fields.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song times it has been gradually neglected; the water fell low, grass grew, and it slowly turned into fields of water shield.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，知杭州蘇軾奏謂：「杭之為州，本江海故地，水泉咸苦，居民零落。

translations.literal: Yuanyou period, Prefect of Hangzhou Su Shi memorial said: "Hang as prefecture, originally river sea old land, springs salty bitter, residents scattered few.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era Su Shi, prefect of Hangzhou, memorialized: "Hangzhou as a prefecture was originally ground of river and sea; its springs were brackish and bitter and the people were sparse.

sentences.zh: 自唐李泌始引湖水作六井，然後民足于水，井邑日富，百萬生聚，待此而食。

translations.literal: From Tang Li Bi first drew lake water made six wells, afterward people sufficient in water, towns daily rich, million lives gathered, rely on this to live.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang times Li Bi first drew lake water to make six wells; afterward the people had enough water, the towns grew daily richer, and a million souls gathered who depend on this to live.

sentences.zh: 今湖狹水淺，六井盡壞，若二十年後，盡為葑田，則舉城之人，復飲咸水，其勢必耗散。

translations.literal: Now lake narrow water shallow, six wells all ruined, if twenty years afterward, all become water-shield fields, then whole city's people, again drink salty water, its momentum must disperse waste.
translations.idiomatic: The lake is now narrow and shallow and the six wells are all ruined. If in twenty years it all becomes fields of water shield, then the people of the whole city will again drink brackish water and the population will inevitably scatter.

sentences.zh: 又放水溉田，瀕湖千頃，可無凶歲。

translations.literal: Again release water irrigate fields, lake margin thousand qing, can have no famine years.
translations.idiomatic: Releasing water also irrigates fields: a thousand qing along the lake may be free of famine years.

sentences.zh: 今雖不及千頃，而下湖數十里間，茭菱谷米，所獲不貲。

translations.literal: Now although not reach thousand qing, yet lower lake several tens li between, water chestnuts lotus grain rice, harvest obtained not small.
translations.idiomatic: Though it is now less than a thousand qing, within several tens of li of the lower lake the yield of water chestnuts, lotus, and grain is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 又西湖深闊，則運河可以取足於湖水，若湖水不足，則必取足于江潮。

translations.literal: Again West Lake deep broad, then Grand Canal can take sufficiency from lake water, if lake water not sufficient, then must take sufficiency from river tide.
translations.idiomatic: Again, if West Lake is deep and broad the canal may draw fully from the lake; if the lake is insufficient it must draw fully from the tidal river.

sentences.zh: 潮之所過，泥沙渾濁，一石五鬥，不出三載，輒調兵夫十余萬開浚。

translations.literal: Where tide passes, mud sand turbid muddy, one stone five dou, within three years not out, then mobilize soldiers laborers hundred thousand-plus open dredge.
translations.idiomatic: Where the tide passes the mud and sand are turbid—five dou of mud in every stone—and within three years more than a hundred thousand soldiers and laborers must be mobilized for dredging.

sentences.zh: 又天下酒官之盛，如杭歲課二十余萬緡，而水泉之用，仰給於湖。

translations.literal: Again under heaven wine monopoly flourishing, like Hang yearly levy two hundred thousand-plus strings, yet spring water use, relies supply on lake.
translations.idiomatic: Again, of the great wine monopolies under heaven, Hangzhou alone levies more than two hundred thousand strings a year, and its water supply depends on the lake.

sentences.zh: 若湖漸淺狹，少不應溝，則當勞人遠取山泉，歲不下二十萬工。」

translations.literal: If lake gradually shallow narrow, slightly not answer ditch, then must labor people far fetch mountain springs, yearly not below two hundred thousand work."
translations.idiomatic: If the lake grows gradually shallow and narrow and falls even slightly short of the channels, people must be sent far to fetch mountain springs at a cost of no less than two hundred thousand work-days a year."

sentences.zh: 因請降度牒減價出賣，募民開治。

translations.literal: Therefore requested issue ordination certificates reduced price sell, recruit people open govern.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked that ordination certificates be issued and sold at reduced price to recruit the people for dredging.

sentences.zh: 禁自今不得請射、侵佔、種植及臠葑為界。

translations.literal: Forbidden from now not allow petition claim, encroach occupy, plant grow and carve water-shield as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: It was forbidden henceforth to petition for claims, encroach, plant crops, or stake out boundaries with cut water shield.

sentences.zh: 以新舊菱蕩課利錢送錢塘縣收掌，謂之開湖司公使庫，以備逐年雇人開葑撩淺。

translations.literal: Take new old water-chestnut ponds tax profit money send Qiantang county receive keep, called Open Lake Office public expense treasury, to prepare year by year hire people open water-shield dredge shallow.
translations.idiomatic: The tax profits from old and new water-chestnut ponds were sent to Qiantang county to be held in what was called the Open Lake Office public treasury, to provide for hiring men each year to clear water shield and dredge the shallows.

sentences.zh: 縣尉以「管勾開湖司公事」系銜。

translations.literal: County captain with "manage Open Lake Office public affairs" attached title.
translations.idiomatic: The county captain bore the attached title "Officer in Charge of Open Lake Office Affairs."

sentences.zh: 軾既開湖，因積葑草為堤，相去數里，橫跨南、北兩山，夾道植柳，林希榜曰「蘇公堤」，行人便之，因為軾立祠堤上。

translations.literal: Shi already opened lake, therefore piled water-shield grass as dike, separated several li, cross span south north two mountains, flanking road planted willows, Lin Xi posted placard called "Lord Su Embankment," travelers convenient it, therefore for Shi established shrine on dike.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi had opened the lake, he piled the dredged water shield into a dike several li in length spanning the southern and northern hills, with willows planted along the road. Lin Xi posted a placard naming it "Lord Su's Embankment." Travelers found it convenient, and a shrine to Shi was built upon the dike.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，以張澄奏請，命臨安府招置廂軍兵士二百人，委錢塘縣尉兼領其事，專一浚湖；

translations.literal: Shaoxing ninth year, on Zhang Cheng memorial request, ordered Lin'an prefecture recruit establish garrison soldiers two hundred men, entrust Qiantang county captain concurrently lead this affair, exclusively dredge lake;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, on Zhang Cheng's petition, Lin'an was ordered to recruit two hundred garrison soldiers, with the Qiantang county captain placed in charge to dredge the lake exclusively;

sentences.zh: 若包占種田，沃以糞土，重寘於法。

translations.literal: If encircle occupy plant fields, enrich with manure soil, heavily punish by law.
translations.idiomatic: if anyone encroached to farm and enriched the soil with manure, heavy penalties were imposed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，守臣湯鵬舉奏請重開。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, defending official Tang Pengju memorial requested again open.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the prefect Tang Pengju memorialized requesting that it be opened anew.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，守臣周淙言：「西湖水面唯務深闊，不容填溢，並引入城內諸井，一城汲用，尤在涓潔。

translations.literal: Qiandao fifth year, defending official Zhou Cong said: "West Lake water surface only strive deep broad, not allow fill overflow, also draw into city within various wells, whole city draw use, especially lies in pure clean.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiandao the prefect Zhou Cong said: "The surface of West Lake must be kept deep and broad and must not be filled or allowed to overflow. It also feeds the wells within the city; the whole city's drawing of water depends above all on its being pure.

sentences.zh: 舊招軍士止有三十餘人，今宜增置撩湖軍兵，以百人為額，專一開撩。

translations.literal: Formerly recruited soldiers only had thirty-plus men, now ought increase establish lake-dredging army soldiers, with hundred men as quota, exclusively open dredge.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers formerly recruited number only a little more than thirty. Lake-dredging troops should now be increased to a quota of one hundred men for exclusive dredging.

sentences.zh: 或有種植茭菱，因而包占，增疊堤岸，坐以違制。」

translations.literal: If have plant grow water chestnuts lotus, therefore encircle occupy, add pile dike banks, sit with violation of regulation."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone plants water chestnuts or lotus and thereby encroaches and builds up the banks, let him be punished for violation of regulations."

sentences.zh: 九年，臨安守臣言：「西湖冒佃侵多，葑茭蔓延，西南一帶，已成平陸。

translations.literal: Ninth year, Lin'an defending official said: "West Lake reckless tenancy encroachments many, water-shield sedge spread extend, southwest one stretch, already became level land.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the prefect of Lin'an said: "Encroachments on West Lake through reckless tenancy are many; water shield and sedge have spread, and the whole southwestern stretch has already become level ground.

sentences.zh: 而瀕湖之民，每以葑草圍裹，種植荷花，駸駸不已。

translations.literal: Yet lake-margin people, each use water-shield grass wrap enclose, plant grow lotus flowers, steadily without stop.
translations.idiomatic: The people along the lake continually wrap plots with water-shield grass and plant lotus, pressing on without cease.

sentences.zh: 恐數十年後，西湖遂淤，將如越之鑒湖，不可復矣。

translations.literal: Fear several tens years afterward, West Lake then silt, will be like Yue's Mirror Lake, cannot again restore.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in several decades West Lake will silt up and become like Mirror Lake in Yue, beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 乞一切芟除，務令淨盡，禁約居民，不得再有圍裹。」

translations.literal: Beg all cut remove, strive make clean exhausted, forbid bind residents, not allow again have wrap enclose."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that all of it be cut away and cleared completely and that the residents be forbidden to enclose plots again."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 臨安運河在城中者，日納潮水，沙泥渾濁，一汛一淤，比屋之民，委棄草壤，因循填塞。

translations.literal: Lin'an Grand Canal in city within, daily receives tidal water, sand mud turbid muddy, one tide one silt, neighboring houses' people, cast away grass soil, follow along fill block.
translations.idiomatic: The stretch of the Grand Canal within Lin'an receives the tide daily; the sand and mud are turbid, and each tide brings silt. The people of every neighboring house cast away grass and soil and, by slow degrees, fill and block the channel.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，守臣蘇軾奏謂：「熙寧中，通判杭州時，父老皆云苦運河淤塞，率三五年常一開浚。

translations.literal: Yuanyou period, defending official Su Shi memorial said: "Xining period, as Vice Prefect of Hangzhou time, elders all said suffered Grand Canal silt block, generally three five years regularly one open dredge.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era the prefect Su Shi memorialized: "During the Xining era, when I was vice prefect of Hangzhou, the elders all said they suffered from the canal's silting and that dredging was needed every three to five years as a rule.

sentences.zh: 不獨勞役兵民，而運河自州前至北郭，穿闤闠中蓋十四五里，每將興工，市肆洶動，公私騷然。

translations.literal: Not only toil soldiers people, yet Grand Canal from prefecture front to North Suburb, pierces market lanes within about fourteen five li, each time about raise work, shops markets turbulent move, public private uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Not only did this toil soldiers and civilians, but the canal from before the prefecture to the North Suburb runs fourteen or fifteen li through the market lanes, and whenever work was about to begin the shops were thrown into turmoil and public and private affairs alike were thrown into uproar.

sentences.zh: 自胥吏、壕砦兵級等，皆能恐喝人戶，或云當於某處置土、某處過泥水，則居者皆有失業之憂。

translations.literal: From clerks and moat-garrison soldiers and the like, all could intimidate and extort households, or say earth must be placed at a certain spot or muddy water must pass a certain spot, so that those who lived there all had fears of losing their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Even clerks, moat-garrison troops, and men of that rank could intimidate and shake down households—claiming that earth had to be dumped here or that muddy water had to be routed there—until every resident feared for his livelihood.

sentences.zh: 既得重賂，又轉而之他。

translations.literal: Having already obtained heavy bribes, they then turned and went elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had pocketed a hefty bribe, they moved on to the next victim.

sentences.zh: 及工役既畢，則房廊、邸舍，作踐狼籍，園圃隙地，例成丘阜，積雨蕩濯，復入河中，居民患厭，未易悉數。

translations.literal: When the labor was finished, then verandas and lodging houses were trampled in disorder, garden plots and vacant spaces routinely became mounds, accumulated rain washed and scoured them back into the river, residents were afflicted and resentful, not easy to enumerate fully.
translations.idiomatic: When the work ended, verandas and lodging houses lay trampled and chaotic; gaps in gardens and empty lots had routinely been heaped into mounds, and when heavy rains came the spoil washed back into the canal—so many grievances among the residents that they cannot all be told.

sentences.zh: 若三五年失開，則公私壅滯，以尺寸水行數百斛舟，人牛力盡，跬步千里，雖監司使命，有數日不能出郭者。

translations.literal: If for three or five years dredging was neglected, then public and private traffic was clogged; with water a finger's depth boats of hundreds of hu capacity were moved, men and oxen exhausted their strength, an inch became a thousand li, and even commissioners on official missions sometimes could not leave the suburb for several days.
translations.idiomatic: If the canal went three or five years without dredging, public and private traffic stalled entirely. Vessels of hundreds of hu had to be poled through water scarcely deeper than a finger's breadth; men and oxen strained to the limit, every step an ordeal; even commissioners on urgent business sometimes could not leave the city outskirts for days.

sentences.zh: 詢其所以頻開屢塞之由，皆云龍山浙江兩閘，泥沙渾濁，積日稍久，便及四五尺，其勢當然，不足怪也。

translations.literal: Inquiring into the reason for frequent dredging and repeated silting, all said that at the two sluices of Longshan and the Zhe River the sand and mud were turbid, and after days accumulated soon reached four or five chi—such was the natural tendency, not enough to be wondered at.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why dredging had to be done again and again, everyone said that at the Longshan and Qiantang sluices the silt was so turbid that in only a few days it piled four or five chi deep—a natural result, nothing surprising.

sentences.zh: 尋剗刷捍江兵士及諸色廂軍，得一千人，七月之間，開浚茅山、鹽橋二河，各十餘里，皆有水八尺。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he mustered river-defense soldiers and various metropolitan garrison troops, obtaining one thousand men, and within the seventh month opened and dredged the Mao and Salt Bridge canals, each more than ten li, all with eight chi of water.
translations.idiomatic: He soon assembled a thousand river-defense soldiers and metropolitan garrison troops and, within the seventh month, dredged the Mao and Salt Bridge canals, each more than ten li long, to a depth of eight chi throughout.

sentences.zh: 自是公私舟船通利，三十年以來，開河未有若此深快者。

translations.literal: From this public and private boats passed freely; in thirty years of dredging the canal there had never been one so deep and satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: From then on public and private vessels passed freely—the deepest and most satisfactory dredging in thirty years.

sentences.zh: 然潮水日至，淤塞猶昔，則三五年間，前功復棄。

translations.literal: Yet the tide came daily and silting was as before, so that within three or five years the previous work was again wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tide still came daily and silting resumed as before, so that within three or five years the earlier labor would be undone.

sentences.zh: 今于鈐轄司前置一閘，每遇潮上，則暫閉此閘，候潮平水清復開，則河過闤闠中者，永無潮水淤塞、開淘騷擾之患。」

translations.literal: Now place a sluice before the Controller-General's office; whenever the tide rises, temporarily close this sluice and wait until the tide levels and the water clears before reopening—then the stretch of canal passing through the market lanes will forever be free of the afflictions of tidal silting and dredging turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed placing a sluice before the Controller-General's office: whenever the tide rose, the gate would be shut until the tide fell and the water cleared; the stretch of canal running through the markets would then forever be spared tidal silting and the turmoil of repeated dredging."

sentences.zh: 詔從其請，民甚便之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his request; the people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted by edict, to the great convenience of the people.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年十一月，宰臣奏開修運河淺澀，帝曰：「可發旁郡廂軍、壯城、捍江之兵，至於廩給之費，則不當吝。」

translations.literal: Shaoxing third year eleventh month, chief ministers memorialized to open and repair the shallow, silted Grand Canal; the emperor said: "May dispatch from neighboring prefectures metropolitan garrison, stronghold, and river-defense troops; as for the cost of grain rations, one should not be sparing."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Shaoxing the chief ministers memorialized to dredge the shallow, silted stretches of the Grand Canal. The emperor said: "Dispatch metropolitan garrison, stronghold, and river-defense troops from the neighboring prefectures. As for grain rations, do not be stinting."

sentences.zh: 宰臣朱勝非等曰：「開河非今急務，而饋餉艱難，為害甚大。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Zhu Shengfei and others said: "Opening the canal is not an urgent task of the present, yet supplying provisions is arduous and the harm is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Ministers Zhu Shengfei and others replied: "Dredging the canal is not the most urgent business now, yet the difficulty of supplying provisions would cause great harm.

sentences.zh: 時方盛寒，役者良苦，臨流居人，侵塞河道者，悉當遷避；

translations.literal: The season was at its coldest; the laborers suffered bitter hardship; residents along the stream whose encroachments blocked the waterway must all be made to relocate;
translations.idiomatic: The season was bitterly cold and the laborers would suffer greatly; residents along the canal who had encroached on and blocked the channel would all have to be relocated;

sentences.zh: 至於畚閘所經，沙泥所積，當預空其處，則居人及富家以僦屋取貲者皆非便，恐議者以為言。」

translations.literal: As for places where dredging baskets and sluices would pass and sand and mud would accumulate, the sites must be cleared in advance—then residents and wealthy families who rented houses for profit would all be inconvenienced; I fear critics would raise objections."
translations.idiomatic: and wherever dredging and sluice work would pass, sand and mud would have to be stored—requiring that sites be cleared in advance, to the great inconvenience of residents and of wealthy families who earned rents from leased houses. Critics would surely object."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「禹卑宮室而盡力於溝洫，浮言何恤焉！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yu made his palace low and devoted his strength to ditches and canals—why worry about idle talk!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yu kept his palace humble and poured his strength into canals—why heed idle talk!"

sentences.zh: 八年，又命守臣張澄發廂軍、壯城兵千人，開浚運河堙塞，以通往來舟楫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again ordered the defending official Zhang Cheng to dispatch a thousand metropolitan garrison and stronghold troops to open and dredge the blocked Grand Canal, so as to clear passage for traveling boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the prefect Zhang Cheng was again ordered to dispatch a thousand metropolitan garrison and stronghold troops to dredge the silted canal and restore passage for boats.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年，守臣吳芾言：「城裏運河，先已措置北梅家橋、仁和倉、斜橋三所作壩，取西湖六處水口通流灌入。

translations.literal: Longxing second year, defending official Wu Bi said: "The canal within the city—measures had already been taken at the three places of North Meijia Bridge, Renhe Granary, and Xie Bridge to build dams and draw from six West Lake outlets to pour in flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longxing the prefect Wu Bi said: "For the canal within the city, dams had already been built at North Meijia Bridge, Renhe Granary, and Xie Bridge, drawing water from six West Lake outlets.

sentences.zh: 府河積水，至望仙橋以南至都亭驛一帶，河道地勢，自昔高峻。

translations.literal: The prefectural canal accumulated water, but from south of Wangxian Bridge to the stretch of Duting Post Station the canal bed's terrain had from old been lofty and steep.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural canal held water, but from south of Wangxian Bridge to Duting Post the bed had always been high and steep.

sentences.zh: 今欲先於望仙橋城外保安閘兩頭作壩，卻于竹車門河南開掘水道，車戽運水，引入保安門通流入城，遂自望仙橋以南開至都亭驛橋，可以通徹積水，以備緩急。

translations.literal: Now we wish first at both ends outside Wangxian Bridge at Bao'an Sluice to build dams, then south of Zhuche Gate River to excavate a waterway, using chain pumps to move water and draw it through Bao'an Gate to flow into the city, and then open from south of Wangxian Bridge to Duting Post Bridge, so that accumulated water may be thoroughly cleared for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: We now propose first building dams at both ends of Bao'an Sluice outside Wangxian Bridge, then excavating a channel south of Zhuche Gate River and using chain pumps to lift water in through Bao'an Gate, and opening the bed from Wangxian Bridge south to Duting Post Bridge so that pooled water can be fully drained in an emergency.

sentences.zh: 計用工四萬。」

translations.literal: The labor was estimated at forty thousand work-days."
translations.idiomatic: Labor was estimated at forty thousand work-days."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 乾道三年六月，知荊南府王炎言：「臨安居民繁夥，河港堙塞，雖屢開導，緣裁減工費，不能迄功。

translations.literal: Qiandao third year sixth month, Jingnan prefect Wang Yan said: "Lin'an's residents are numerous and crowded; river channels are blocked. Although dredging has been done repeatedly, because work expenses were cut it could not be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Qiandao Wang Yan, prefect of Jingnan, said: "Lin'an is densely populated and its channels are choked. Dredging has been attempted many times, but cuts to the budget kept the work from completion.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗措置開河錢十萬緡，乞候農暇，特詔有司，用此專充開河支費，庶幾河渠復通，公私為利。」

translations.literal: Your subject once arranged one hundred thousand strings for canal opening; I beg that when farm work slackens a special edict instruct the responsible offices to use this solely for canal-opening expenses, so that perhaps the waterways may be restored and public and private interests alike benefit."
translations.idiomatic: I have set aside one hundred thousand strings for dredging. I beg that when the farming season slackens Your Majesty issue a special edict directing the offices to use these funds solely for dredging, so that the waterways may be restored to the benefit of all."

sentences.zh: 上俞其請。

translations.literal: The emperor assented to his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 四年，守臣周淙出公帑錢招集遊民，開浚城內外河，疏通淤塞，人以治辦稱之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, defending official Zhou Cong spent public treasury money to recruit vagrant laborers, opened and dredged the rivers inside and outside the city, cleared silting, and people praised him for effective administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Prefect Zhou Cong spent government funds to recruit migrant laborers, dredged the rivers inside and outside the city, cleared the silt, and won renown for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，兩浙漕臣趙磻老言：「臨安府長安閘至許村巡檢司一帶，漕河淺澀，請出錢米，發兩岸人戶出力開浚。」

translations.literal: Chunxi second year, Two-Zhe transport commissioner Zhao Panlao said: "From Chang'an Sluice in Lin'an prefecture to the Xucun inspection post stretch, the transport canal is shallow and silted; I request to provide money and grain and mobilize households on both banks to contribute labor for dredging."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunxi the Two-Zhe transport commissioner Zhao Panlao said: "From Chang'an Sluice to the Xucun inspection post the transport canal is shallow and silted. I request funds and grain to mobilize households on both banks for dredging."

sentences.zh: 又言：「欲于通江橋置板閘，遇城中河水淺涸，啟板納潮，繼即下板，固護水勢，不得通舟；

translations.literal: He also said: "We wish to place a board sluice at Tongjiang Bridge; when the city river is shallow and dry, raise the boards to admit the tide, then immediately lower them to secure the water level and not allow boats to pass;
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed: "Place a board sluice at Tongjiang Bridge: when the city river runs low, raise the boards to admit the tide and then lower them at once to hold the water level—boats would not pass while the boards were down;

sentences.zh: 若河水不乏，即收閘板，聽舟楫往還為便。」

translations.literal: if the river water is not wanting, then remove the sluice boards and allow boats to come and go for convenience."
translations.idiomatic: when the river is full, remove the boards and allow vessels to pass freely."

sentences.zh: 七年，守臣吳淵言：「萬松嶺兩旁古渠，多被權勢及有司公吏之家造屋侵佔，及內砦前石橋、都亭驛橋南北河道，居民多拋糞土瓦礫，以致填塞，流水不通。

translations.literal: Seventh year, defending official Wu Yuan said: "The ancient canals on both sides of Wansong Ridge have mostly been built upon and encroached by powerful families and the homes of government clerks; and at the stone bridge before the inner encampment and north and south of Duting Post Bridge the residents cast much dung, soil, and rubble, so that filling and blocking occurred and flowing water could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Prefect Wu Yuan said: "The ancient canals flanking Wansong Ridge have largely been built over by powerful families and by officials' households; at the stone bridge before the inner encampment and along the channel north and south of Duting Post Bridge residents dump dung, earth, and rubble until the flow is choked off.

sentences.zh: 今欲分委兩通判監督，地分廂巡，逐時點檢，勿令侵佔並拋颺糞土。

translations.literal: Now we wish to assign two assistant prefects to supervise, with ward patrols in each area inspecting from time to time, not allowing encroachment or casting of dung and soil.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed placing two assistant prefects in charge, with ward patrols to inspect regularly and forbid encroachment and dumping.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，若不淤塞，各減一年磨勘；

translations.literal: At the end of their terms, if there is no silting, each shall have one year shaved from their merit review;
translations.idiomatic: At term's end, if the channels remained unblocked, each would receive one year credit on his merit review;

sentences.zh: 違，展一年，以示勸懲。」

translations.literal: if violated, extend by one year, to show encouragement and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: if not, one year would be added—a reward and a penalty."

sentences.zh: 十四年七月，不雨，臣僚言：「竊見奉口至北新橋三十六里，斷港絕潢，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year seventh month, no rain, a courtier said: "I have observed that from Fengkou to Beixin Bridge for thirty-six li the waterways are severed and cut off—nowhere worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, during a drought, a courtier said: "From Fengkou to Beixin Bridge, thirty-six li of waterway are cut off and choked—nowhere worse.

sentences.zh: 今宜開浚，使通客船，以平谷直。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to open and dredge, so that traveling boats may pass and transport costs may be eased."
translations.idiomatic: It should be dredged so that passenger boats can pass and freight rates may be reduced."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 鹽官海水

translations.literal: Yanguan seawater
translations.idiomatic: The Seawaters of Yanguan

sentences.zh: 鹽官海水：嘉定十二年，臣僚言：「鹽官去海三十餘里，舊無海患，縣以鹽灶頗盛，課利易登。

translations.literal: Yanguan seawater: Jiading twelfth year, a courtier said: "Yanguan is more than thirty li from the sea and formerly had no sea calamity; the county's salt pans were quite flourishing and tax revenue was easily collected.
translations.idiomatic: The seawaters of Yanguan: In the twelfth year of Jiading a courtier said: "Yanguan lies more than thirty li from the sea and had never known coastal disaster; with its salt pans thriving, tax revenue was easily collected.

sentences.zh: 去歲海水泛漲，湍激橫沖，沙岸每一潰裂，嘗數十丈。

translations.literal: Last year the sea water spread and rose; rushing torrents struck across; each time the sand bank breached the crack was often several tens of zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the sea surged and tore across the shore; each breach of the sand bank ran several tens of zhang.

sentences.zh: 日復一日，浸入鹵地，蘆州港瀆，蕩為一壑。

translations.literal: Day after day it soaked into the salt flats; Lu harbor and channels were washed into a single gully.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day it ate into the salt flats; Lu Harbor and its channels were scoured into a single hollow.

sentences.zh: 今聞潮勢深入，逼近居民。

translations.literal: Now I hear the tide's force has penetrated deep and presses close upon the residents.
translations.idiomatic: Now the tide is said to have driven inland and to be pressing upon the settlements.

sentences.zh: 萬一春水驟漲，怒濤奔湧，海風佐之，則呼吸蕩出，百里之民，寧不俱葬魚腹乎？

translations.literal: If by chance spring waters suddenly rise, angry billows surge, and sea winds assist them, then in a breath they would sweep out—would not the people for a hundred li all be buried in fishes' bellies together?
translations.idiomatic: If spring floods should suddenly rise and raging surf, aided by sea winds, should sweep inland in a breath, would not every soul for a hundred li be drowned together?

sentences.zh: 況京畿赤縣，密邇都城。

translations.literal: Moreover it is a capital-district red-banner county, close beside the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this is a privileged county of the capital region, close beside the court.

sentences.zh: 內有二十五里塘，直通長安閘，上徹臨平，下接崇德，漕運往來，客船絡繹，兩岸田畝，無非沃壤。

translations.literal: Within it is the Twenty-five-li Embankment, running straight to Chang'an Sluice, reaching up to Linping and down to Chongde; transport grain comes and goes, passenger boats throng in succession, and fields on both banks are all rich soil.
translations.idiomatic: Within the county runs the Twenty-five-li Embankment, linking Chang'an Sluice, reaching Linping above and Chongde below; grain transport and passenger traffic move in constant stream, and the fields on both banks are all rich farmland.

sentences.zh: 若海水徑入於塘，不惟民田有咸水渰沒之患，而裏河堤岸，亦將有潰裂之憂。

translations.literal: If sea water directly enters the embankment, not only would civilian fields suffer the affliction of salt water flooding and drowning, but the inner river's dikes and banks would also have fears of breach and rupture.
translations.idiomatic: If the sea should break directly into the embankment, not only would the fields face inundation by salt water, but the inner river's dikes would be in danger of giving way.

sentences.zh: 乞下浙西諸司，條具築捺之策，務使捍堤堅壯，土脈充實，不為怒潮所沖。」

translations.literal: I beg that the Western Zhe offices be ordered to draw up plans for building and blocking, striving to make the sea-defense dikes firm and strong, their earth solid and full, and not washed by raging tides."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Western Zhe offices be ordered to submit plans for embankment works, so that the sea dikes may stand firm and solid and not be shattered by raging tides."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十五年，都省言：鹽官縣海塘沖決，命浙西提舉劉垕專任其事。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, the Secretariat said: The sea wall of Yanguan county was breached; Liu Huang of the Western Zhe intendant commission was ordered to take sole charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Secretariat reported that the sea wall at Yanguan had been breached and appointed Liu Huang, Western Zhe intendant, to take sole charge.

sentences.zh: 既而垕言：

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Huang said:
translations.idiomatic: Huang soon reported:

sentences.zh: 縣東接海鹽，西距仁和，北抵崇德、德清，境連平江、嘉興、湖州；

translations.literal: East the county adjoins Haiyan, west it borders Renhe, north it reaches Chongde and Deqing, its territory linking Pingjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou;
translations.idiomatic: East the county adjoins Haiyan, west it borders Renhe, north it reaches Chongde and Deqing, and its territory links Pingjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou;

sentences.zh: 南瀕大海元與縣治相去四十餘里。

translations.literal: south it faced the great sea, formerly more than forty li from the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: south it faced the open sea, once more than forty li from the county seat.

sentences.zh: 數年以來，水失故道，早晚兩潮，奔沖向北，遂致縣南四十餘里盡淪為海。

translations.literal: For several years the water lost its old course; morning and evening tides rushed north, so that more than forty li south of the county were entirely swallowed by the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the water lost its old channels; morning and evening tides charged north, and more than forty li south of the county have been wholly lost to the sea.

sentences.zh: 近縣之南，元有捍海古塘亙二十里。

translations.literal: South of the nearby county seat there had formerly been an ancient sea-defense embankment stretching twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: South of the county seat there had once been an ancient sea wall twenty li long.

sentences.zh: 今東西兩段，並已淪毀，侵入縣兩旁又各三四里，止存中間古塘十餘里。

translations.literal: Now the eastern and western sections have both been destroyed and lost; the sea has encroached three or four li on each flank of the county, and only some ten-odd li of the middle ancient embankment remain.
translations.idiomatic: Its eastern and western sections have now been destroyed; the sea has eaten three or four li into each side of the county, and only some ten li of the central stretch remain.

sentences.zh: 萬一水勢沖激不已，不惟鹽官一縣不可復存，而向北地勢卑下，所慮咸流入蘇、秀、湖三州等處，則田畝不可種植，大為利害。

translations.literal: If by chance the water's force should strike without cease, not only would Yanguan county alone be unable to survive, but northward the terrain is low—what is feared is salt water flowing into Suzhou, Xiuzhou, Huzhou, and the like, so that fields could not be planted—a matter of great harm and benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If the sea should keep driving inland, not only would Yanguan cease to exist; to the north the land lies low, and salt water might reach Suzhou, Xiuzhou, and Huzhou so that fields could no longer be cultivated—a calamity of the first magnitude.

sentences.zh: 詳今日之患，大概有二：一曰陸地淪毀，二曰鹹潮泛溢。

translations.literal: Examining today's afflictions, there are broadly two: first, land destroyed and lost; second, salt tide spreading and overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Today's disasters fall broadly into two: loss of land to the sea, and the spreading of salt tides.

sentences.zh: 陸地淪毀者，固無力可施；

translations.literal: As for land destroyed and lost, truly nothing can be done;
translations.idiomatic: For land already lost to the sea nothing can be done;

sentences.zh: 鹹潮泛溢者，乃因捍海古塘沖損，遇大潮必盤越流注北向，宜築土塘以捍鹹潮。

translations.literal: as for salt tide spreading, it is because the ancient sea wall was breached; when great tides come they must coil over and pour northward—an earthen embankment should be built to repel the salt tide.
translations.idiomatic: but the salt tides spread because the ancient sea wall has been breached—great tides spill over and pour north. An earthen embankment should be built to hold them back.

sentences.zh: 所築塘基址，南北各有兩處：在縣東近南則為六十里鹹塘，近北則為袁花塘；

translations.literal: For sites where embankments are to be built, north and south each have two places: east of the county near the south is the Sixty-li Salt Embankment, near the north is Yuanhua Embankment;
translations.idiomatic: For new embankments there are two sites on each flank: east of the county, to the south the Sixty-li Salt Embankment and to the north Yuanhua Embankment;

sentences.zh: 在縣西近南亦曰鹹塘，近北則為淡塘。

translations.literal: west of the county near the south is also called Salt Embankment, near the north is Freshwater Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: west of the county, the southern site is likewise the Salt Embankment and the northern the Freshwater Embankment.

sentences.zh: 亦嘗驗兩處土色虛實，則袁花塘、淡塘差勝鹹塘，且各近裏，未至與海潮為敵。

translations.literal: We have also tested the solidity of the earth at both places; Yuanhua and Freshwater embankments are somewhat superior to Salt Embankment, and each lies nearer inland, not yet reaching confrontation with the sea tide.
translations.idiomatic: Tests of the soil showed Yuanhua and Freshwater embankments to be somewhat better than the Salt Embankment, and both lie farther inland, not yet fully exposed to the open tide.

sentences.zh: 勢當東就袁花塘、西就淡塘修築，則可以禦縣東鹹潮盤溢之患。

translations.literal: The situation requires building east at Yuanhua Embankment and west at Freshwater Embankment, then one can repel the affliction of salt tide coiling and overflowing east of the county.
translations.idiomatic: The east should be reinforced at Yuanhua Embankment and the west at Freshwater Embankment, which would hold back the salt tides surging from the east.

sentences.zh: 其縣西一帶淡塘，連縣治左右，共五十餘里，合先修築。

translations.literal: The stretch of Freshwater Embankment west of the county, connected to both sides of the county seat, totals more than fifty li and should be repaired first.
translations.idiomatic: The Freshwater Embankment west of the county, running fifty-odd li along both sides of the seat, should be repaired first.

sentences.zh: 兼縣南去海一里余，幸而古塘尚存，縣治民居，盡在其中，未可棄之度外。

translations.literal: Moreover south of the county it is a little more than one li to the sea; fortunately the ancient embankment still remains, and the county seat and people's dwellings are all within it—it cannot be abandoned outside consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the county seat lies scarcely more than a li from the sea; fortunately the ancient wall still stands and the seat and settlements all lie within it—this must not be neglected.

sentences.zh: 今將見管樁石，就古塘稍加工築疊一里許，為防護縣治之計。

translations.literal: Now using the piles and stone on hand, upon the ancient embankment we shall somewhat add work to build and stack about one li, as a plan to protect the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Available timber and stone will be used to strengthen the ancient wall for about one li to shield the county seat.

sentences.zh: 其縣東民戶，日築六十里鹹塘。

translations.literal: The households east of the county are daily building the Sixty-li Salt Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: East of the county the households are daily raising the Sixty-li Salt Embankment.

sentences.zh: 萬一又為海潮沖損，當計用樁木修築袁花塘以捍之。

translations.literal: If by chance it is again struck and damaged by sea tides, we should plan to use piles and timber to build Yuanhua Embankment to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: If the sea should breach it again, piles and timber should be used to build up Yuanhua Embankment as a second line of defense.

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor considered it correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 明州水

translations.literal: Ming prefecture waters
translations.idiomatic: The Waters of Ming Prefecture

sentences.zh: 明州水：紹興五年，明州守臣李光奏：「明、越陂湖，專溉農田。

translations.literal: Ming prefecture waters: Shaoxing fifth year, Ming prefecture defending official Li Guang memorialized: "Ming and Yue's reservoir lakes exclusively irrigate farmland.
translations.idiomatic: The waters of Ming Prefecture: In the fifth year of Shaoxing Prefect Li Guang of Ming memorialized: "The reservoir lakes of Ming and Yue exist solely to irrigate farmland.

sentences.zh: 自慶曆中，始有盜湖為田者，三司使切責漕臣，嚴立法禁。

translations.literal: From the Qingli era there began those who stole lakes for fields; the Three Departments commissioner sternly reproached the transport officials and strictly established legal prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qingli era people began encroaching on the lakes for fields; the commissioner of the Three Departments rebuked the transport officials and imposed strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 宣和以來，王仲薿守越，樓異守明，創為應奉，始廢湖為田，自是歲有水旱之患。

translations.literal: From Xuanhe onward, Wang Zhongyi guarded Yue and Lou Yi guarded Ming; they created tribute projects and first converted lakes to fields—from then on there were flood and drought calamities every year.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanhe, Wang Zhongyi as prefect of Yue and Lou Yi as prefect of Ming launched corvée tribute projects, first draining the lakes for fields—after which flood and drought returned year after year.

sentences.zh: 乞行廢罷，盡復為湖。

translations.literal: I beg to abolish and revoke these projects and wholly restore them as lakes.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that these projects be abolished and the lakes fully restored.

sentences.zh: 如江東、西之圩田，蘇、秀之圍田，皆當講究興復。」

translations.literal: Such as the polder fields east and west of the river, and the encircled fields of Suzhou and Xiuzhou—all should be studied for restoration."
translations.idiomatic: The polders of Jiangdong and Jiangxi and the embanked fields of Suzhou and Xiuzhou should likewise be reviewed for restoration."

sentences.zh: 詔逐路轉運司相度聞奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered transport commissions in each circuit to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the transport commissions of each circuit to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，守臣張津言：「東錢湖容受七十二溪，方圓廣闊八百頃，傍山為固，疊石為塘八十里。

translations.literal: Qiandao fifth year, defending official Zhang Jin said: "East Qian Lake receives seventy-two streams, four hundred eighty hectares in area, firm with mountains at its side, stones piled into an embankment eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiandao Prefect Zhang Jin said: "East Qian Lake collects seventy-two streams, covers eight hundred qing, is braced by mountains, and is enclosed by a stone embankment eighty li long.

sentences.zh: 自唐天寶三年，縣令陸南金開廣之。

translations.literal: From Tang Tianbao third year the county magistrate Lu Nanjin opened and expanded it.
translations.idiomatic: It was opened and enlarged in the third year of Tianbao of Tang by Magistrate Lu Nanjin.

sentences.zh: 國朝天禧元年，郡守李夷庚重修之。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's Tianxi first year the prefect Li Yigeng rebuilt it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi of our dynasty Prefect Li Yigeng rebuilt it.

sentences.zh: 中有四閘七堰，凡遇旱涸，開閘放水，溉田五十萬畝。

translations.literal: Within it are four sluices and seven weirs; whenever drought and drying occur, the sluices are opened to release water and irrigate five hundred thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: It has four sluices and seven weirs; in drought the gates are opened to irrigate five hundred thousand mu of fields.

sentences.zh: 比因豪民於湖塘淺岸漸次包占，種植菱荷，障塞湖水。

translations.literal: Recently because powerful families on the lake bank's shallow shores gradually encircled and occupied plots, planting water chestnuts and lotus, they blocked and obstructed the lake water.
translations.idiomatic: Lately powerful families have gradually encroached on the shallow shores, planting water chestnuts and lotus and choking the lake.

sentences.zh: 紹興十八年，雖曾檢舉約束，盡罷請佃。

translations.literal: Shaoxing eighteenth year, although violations were reported and constrained, all rental tenancy was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Shaoxing encroachments were investigated and all leases were revoked.

sentences.zh: 歲久菱根蔓延，滲塞水脈，致妨蓄水；

translations.literal: Over years water-chestnut roots spread, seeping and blocking the water channels, causing harm to water storage;
translations.idiomatic: Over the years water-chestnut roots have spread, choking the channels and impairing storage;

sentences.zh: 兼塘岸間有低塌處，若不淘浚修築，不惟浸失水利，兼恐塘埂相繼摧毀。

translations.literal: moreover between embankment banks there are low, collapsed places—if dredging and repair are not done, not only will water benefits be lost by seepage, but I also fear the embankment ridges will be destroyed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: and there are sunken stretches along the embankment. Without dredging and repair, irrigation will fail and the dikes may collapse one after another.

sentences.zh: 乞候農隙趁時開鑿，因得土修治埂岸，實為兩便。」

translations.literal: I beg to wait for a farming interval and take the season to open and excavate, thereby obtaining earth to repair the ridge banks—a real double convenience."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that dredging be done in the farming slack season, using the spoil to repair the banks—a double benefit."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 鄞縣水

translations.literal: Yin county waters
translations.idiomatic: The Waters of Yin County

sentences.zh: 鄞縣水：嘉定十四年，慶元府言：「鄞縣水自四明諸山溪澗會至他山，置堰小涇，下江入河。

translations.literal: Yin county waters: Jiading fourteenth year, Qingyuan prefecture said: "Yin county's waters gather from the streams and ravines of the Siming mountains to Tashan, where a weir and small channel are set, flowing down the river into the main stream.
translations.idiomatic: The waters of Yin County: In the fourteenth year of Jiading Qingyuan prefecture reported: "Yin County's water gathers from the Siming mountains at Tashan, where a weir and small channel direct it down to the river.

sentences.zh: 所入上河之水，專溉民田，其利甚博。

translations.literal: The water entering the upper river exclusively irrigates the people's fields; its benefit is very broad.
translations.idiomatic: The water entering the upper channel irrigates the fields alone, to great benefit.

sentences.zh: 比因淤塞，堰上山觜少有溪水流入上河。

translations.literal: Recently because of silting, at the mountain spur on the weir only a little stream water flows into the upper river.
translations.idiomatic: Lately silting has left only a trickle from the mountain spur above the weir into the upper channel.

sentences.zh: 自春徂夏不雨，令官吏發卒開淘沙觜及浚港汊，又於堰上壘疊沙石，逼使溪流兗入上河。

translations.literal: From spring through summer there was no rain; officials were ordered to dispatch soldiers to open and scour the sand spur and dredge harbor branches, and on the weir stones and sand were piled to force the stream to pour into the upper river.
translations.idiomatic: With no rain from spring through summer, officials dispatched laborers to scour the sand spur and dredge the branches, and piled sand and stone on the weir to force the stream into the upper channel.

sentences.zh: 其他山水入府城南門一帶，有碶閘三所：曰烏金，曰積瀆，曰行春。

translations.literal: Other mountain waters entering the stretch by the prefecture city's south gate have three sluice-gates: called Wujin, Jidu, and Xingchun.
translations.idiomatic: Other mountain streams entering by the south gate of the prefectural city pass three sluice-gates: Wujin, Jidu, and Xingchun.

sentences.zh: 烏金碶又名上水碶，昔因倒損，遂捺為壩，以致淤沙在河，或遇溪流聚湧，時復沖倒所捺壩，走泄水源。

translations.literal: Wujin sluice is also called Upper-water Sluice; formerly because it collapsed it was pressed into a dam, causing silt and sand in the river; when stream water gathers and surges, sometimes the pressed dam is washed down again and the water source runs off.
translations.idiomatic: Wujin Sluice, also called Upper-water Sluice, once collapsed and was blocked into a dam, leaving the channel silted; when streams surge they sometimes burst the dam and waste the headwaters.

sentences.zh: 行春橋又名南石碶，碶面石板之下，歲久損壞空虛，每受潮水，演溢奔突，山于石縫，以致鹹潮盡入上河。

translations.literal: Xingchun Bridge is also called South Stone Sluice; beneath the sluice-face stone slabs, after years damage left them hollow; whenever tidal water came, it overflowed and rushed, mounting through stone crevices, so that salt tide entirely entered the upper river.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchun Bridge, also called South Stone Sluice, has hollow slabs beneath its face; each tide wells up through the cracks and salt water floods the upper channel.

sentences.zh: 其縣東管有道士堰，至白鶴橋一帶，河港堙塞；

translations.literal: East of the county under its jurisdiction is Daoshi Weir; from there to Baihe Bridge the river channels are blocked;
translations.idiomatic: East of the county at Daoshi Weir the channels as far as Baihe Bridge are choked;

sentences.zh: 又有朱賴堰，與行春等碶相連，堰下江流通徹大海。

translations.literal: there is also Zhulai Weir, connected with Xingchun and other sluices; below the weir the river flows through to the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhulai Weir, linked to Xingchun and the other gates, whose channel below runs clear to the sea.

sentences.zh: 今春闕雨，上河乾淺，堰身塌損，以致鹹潮透入上河，使農民不敢車注溉田。

translations.literal: This spring rain was lacking; the upper river was dry and shallow, the weir body collapsed and damaged, so that salt tide penetrated into the upper river and farmers dared not use water-wheels to pour and irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: This spring's drought left the upper channel shallow and the weirs broken, so salt tide seeps in and farmers dare not lift water to irrigate.

sentences.zh: 乞修砌上水、烏金諸處壩堰，仍選清強能幹職官，專一提督。」

translations.literal: I beg to repair and rebuild the dams and weirs at Upper-water, Wujin, and the like, and also select a competent, able official to supervise exclusively."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the dams and weirs at Upper-water, Wujin, and elsewhere be rebuilt, and a capable official appointed to supervise."

sentences.zh: 潤州水

translations.literal: Run prefecture waters
translations.idiomatic: The Waters of Run Prefecture

sentences.zh: 潤州水：紹興七年，兩浙轉運使向子諲言：「鎮江府呂城、夾岡，形勢高仰，因春夏不雨，官漕艱勤。

translations.literal: Run prefecture waters: Shaoxing seventh year, Two-Zhe transport commissioner Xiang Ziyin said: "Zhenjiang prefecture's Lücheng and Jiagang, their terrain lofty and elevated; because spring and summer had no rain, official transport grain was arduously strained.
translations.idiomatic: The waters of Run Prefecture: In the seventh year of Shaoxing the Two-Zhe transport commissioner Xiang Ziyin said: "At Lücheng and Jiagang in Zhenjiang the bed lies high; with no rain through spring and summer, official grain transport has grown arduous.

sentences.zh: 尋遣官屬李澗詢究練湖本末，始知此湖在唐永泰間已廢而復興。

translations.literal: Shortly he dispatched subordinate official Li Jian to inquire into the origins of Lian Lake and first learned that this lake in Tang Yongtai had already been abandoned and then revived.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent Li Jian to investigate Lian Lake and learned that it had been abandoned and restored as early as the Yongtai era of Tang.

sentences.zh: 今堤岸弛禁，致有侵佃冒決，故湖水不能瀦蓄，舟楫不通，公私告病。

translations.literal: Now the dikes and banks have relaxed prohibitions, leading to encroaching tenancy and illicit breaches, so the lake water cannot be dammed and stored, boats cannot pass, and public and private interests alike complain of affliction.
